title: temp_core cold-start branch selection (EN released after supply is up, DR-002 ordering): transient supply ramp from 0 V across the full PVT matrix
claim: Issue #22 -- NOT a spec claim (spec/target-spec.md does not exist yet, spec/porting-plan.md Sec4 item 4). Companion to sim/temp-core-startup/ (scenario A: EN tied high through the whole power-up ramp). This experiment exercises the EN axis temp_core has and bias_core does not (issue #22's own scope): VDD ramps from 0 V exactly as in sim/temp-core-startup/, but EN is held LOW until well after VDD has completed its ramp and settled, then released -- the DR-002 startup ordering temp_core will actually see once temp_por_top exists and drives EN from RESETn (which only deasserts after POR has already released, i.e. supply already up). Substantiates that temp_core's own startup kick still clears the degenerate zero-current branch when enabled LATE, at every point of the full 45-point PVT matrix, not just when EN was asserted for the whole ramp.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

measurements.name: ptat
measurements.note: Same window as sim/temp-core-startup/'s own ptat measurement (see that manifest for the full derivation) -- settled PTAT at t=tstop, open circuit, generous harness-liveness band around design/temp_core.md's own untrimmed DC spot-check table, NOT a spec claim.

measurements.name: ptat_settled
measurements.note: Settling guard, same convention as sim/temp-core-startup/ and sim/bias-core-startup/: PTAT must move less than 1 mV over the last 100 output steps (1 ms of the 10 ms window), well past both the 100 us supply ramp and the 350 us EN release at every corner.

measurements.name: ctat
measurements.note: Same window as sim/temp-core-startup/'s own ctat measurement.

measurements.name: ctat_settled
measurements.note: Settling guard for CTAT, same convention as ptat_settled.

measurements.name: na
measurements.note: Physicality guard (sim/README.md Branch selection rule 4), same as sim/temp-core-startup/'s own na measurement: XDUT.NA is one of the two error-amplifier/DeltaVBE loop nodes internal to temp_core. Bound is the rails plus about a volt of margin (VSS - 1 V .. VDD + 1 V, using the matrix's own 3.63 V supply ceiling as the fixed upper number) -- a false convergence to a degenerate/non-physical branch fails this loudly instead of reading as a plausible number.

measurements.name: nb
measurements.note: Same rail-bound physicality guard as na, on the loop's other DeltaVBE node.

measurements.name: isup
measurements.note: Total quiescent supply current at t=tstop (bias_core + temp_core together, both drawing from V1; EN's own source V2 carries no rail current). Same bound and same rationale as sim/temp-core-startup/'s own isup measurement -- the sign (via the leading '-') rejects the non-physical negative-supply-current artifact this experiment's cold-start method exists to avoid.

measurements.name: bias_ok
measurements.note: bias_core's own settle flag, read from the XBIAS instance this testbench needs to drive IBIAS -- same rationale as sim/temp-core-startup/'s own bias_ok measurement.

spread_checks.note: Corner-blindness guard, same convention as sim/temp-core-startup/'s own spread check.

notes: Analyses list carries one non-analysis control line (`let nlast = length(v(ptat))-1`), same pattern as sim/temp-core-startup/ and sim/bias-core-startup/.

This is the ONLY difference from sim/temp-core-startup/: V2 (EN's own source) is a PWL held at 0 V from t=0 through 'ten_start' (300 us, well after V1's own 100 us VDD ramp has completed and the supply has been flat for 200 us), then ramps to 'vsup' by 'ten_end' (350 us) and holds to 'tstop'. Everything else -- DUT wiring, V1's own VDD ramp, measurements, deck options -- is identical to sim/temp-core-startup/ by construction, so a difference between the two records' results is attributable to EN's timing and nothing else.

Same reltol/integration-method rationale as sim/temp-core-startup/: method=gear + trtol=50 (ngspice defaults: trapezoidal, trtol=7) is what makes the combined bias_core+temp_core cold start tractable in wall time (verified empirically per corner, not assumed), and this deck does NOT carry sim/bias-core-startup/'s own reltol=1e-4 tightening for the same measured performance reason -- the na/nb rail-bound and isup-sign measurements are the guard against a false convergence at the default tolerance, not the tolerance itself.

Ramp rate for VDD is fixed at 'vsup'/'tramp' = ~30 kV/s (100 us 0->3.3 V) for every corner, same single representative ramp as sim/bias-core-startup/ and sim/temp-core-startup/ -- not ramp-rate coverage (that is the POR block's own testbenches, spec/porting-plan.md Sec3.3 / root CLAUDE.md). EN's own release edge ('ten_end' - 'ten_start' = 50 us) is likewise one representative edge rate, not a swept axis.

`uic` skips the initial operating-point solve entirely and integrates forward from all-zero initial conditions on every node in the circuit (both XBIAS and XDUT), which is what makes this a physical cold start rather than a solver-seeded one -- EN itself also starts at 0 V via V2's own PWL, consistent with a real disabled-at-power-up condition.
